about.title: Bruno Abreu
about.subtitle: Full-Stack Developer and Information Systems and Economics graduate focused on Cybersecurity, AppSec, and SOC.
about.bio1: I'm Bruno Abreu, a Full-Stack Developer and Information Systems and Economics graduate focused on Cybersecurity, AppSec, and SOC. I completed the ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC) Official Training and am preparing for the CompTIA Security+ exam.
about.bio2: I created DetonaDev Cyber Lab to document my practical studies in Linux, networks, firewall, logs, SOC, incident response, and tools used in security environments. The goal is to record the learning process transparently, technically, and objectively — showing not just commands, but also the reasoning behind each configuration, diagnosis, and solution.
about.bio3: My professional experience includes web projects, automation, published apps, and technology applied to business. This background strengthens my cybersecurity studies with a practical understanding of how systems work, where they can fail, and how to protect information in real environments.
about.certValue: ISC2 CC Official Training - completed | CompTIA Security+ - in preparation

footer.tagline: Practical studies in Cybersecurity, Linux, Networks, and SOC.

1.title: Remote access via SSH
1.description: Remote access setup between MacBook and Ubuntu via OpenSSH. Concepts of IP, ports, SSH service, and connectivity diagnostics.

2.title: Firewall with UFW
2.description: Configuration and understanding of the UFW firewall on Ubuntu. Inbound and outbound rules, port opening, and access control best practices.

3.title: Authentication logs
3.description: Analysis of SSH authentication logs on Linux. Understanding login events, failures, source IPs, and the importance of logs for SOC.

4.title: Port scanning with Nmap
4.description: Using Nmap to identify open ports and exposed services on local network machines.

5.title: Traffic analysis with Wireshark
5.description: Packet capture and analysis on a local network. Observing protocols such as ICMP, DNS, and TCP.

6.title: Basic monitoring with Wazuh
6.description: Basic installation and configuration of Wazuh as a SIEM for security event monitoring.
